Q: Protein structure visualization A:

I think Pymol is not free anymore since it has to be purchased from Schrödinger. Couple of free programs: - JMol (bad!! don't use that except if you have no other choices) - PyMol (if you are academic) - Yasara - Discovery studio (Accelrys) - RasMol (No longer maintained) - VMD (the best program for visualizing trajectories). Very powerful but I never used it.

I don't know if you can do scripting in all of them.

I work a lot with PyMol and I did some plug in. The only limit is that you can use it as a viewer but nothing else. For example, you can not get an information by clicking on an atom.

good luck

Q: Python / PyQt6 app crashes while loading image thumbnails A:

Fix for PyQt6 threading crash: Don't pass QModelIndex to workers

The random crashes you are experiencing are a classic symptom of memory corruption when working with Qt threads. While the message QThread: Destroyed while thread is still running is a warning about improper cleanup , the actual crash is happening because you are passing a QModelIndex to a background thread.

In PyQt6, QModelIndex objects (and most GUI/Model objects) are not thread-safe. They should never be passed to, or referenced in, any thread other than the main GUI thread. When your ThumbnailLoader worker tries to use that index while the main model is still active, it leads to undefined behavior and immediate crashes.

How to fix it robustly:

  1. Pass only primitive data: Modify your signals to send only the row (int) and the file path (str). These are safe to pass between threads.

  2. Reconstruct the index in the main thread: Once the worker finished loading the image, it should emit the row number back. The model then uses self.index(row) to update itself.

  3. Proper Thread Cleanup: Ensure the thread stops before the object is destroyed to avoid the "Destroyed while running" warning.

Here are the key changes for your code:

class ImageBrowserModel(QtCore.QAbstractListModel):
    # Change signal to use (int, str) for thread safety
    load_thumbnail = QtCore.pyqtSignal(int, str)

    def data(self, index, role):
        if not index.isValid(): return
        image = self._list[index.row()]
        
        if role == QtCore.Qt.ItemDataRole.DecorationRole:
            if image["thumbnail"] is None:
                if not image["thumbnail_loading"]:
                    image["thumbnail_loading"] = True
                    # Use os.path.join for cross-platform compatibility
                    full_path = os.path.join(self._path, image["filename"])
                    # Emit ONLY the row and path
                    self.load_thumbnail.emit(index.row(), full_path)
                return self.placeholder_image
            return image["thumbnail"]

    @QtCore.pyqtSlot(int, QtGui.QImage)
    def thumbnail_loaded(self, row, image):
        if 0 <= row < len(self._list):
            self._list[row]["thumbnail"] = image
            self._list[row]["thumbnail_loading"] = False
            # Reconstruct the index safely on the main thread
            idx = self.index(row)
            self.dataChanged.emit(idx, idx)

    # Proper cleanup to stop the warning
    def __del__(self):
        if self.thumbnail_loader_thread.isRunning():
            self.thumbnail_loader_thread.quit()
            self.thumbnail_loader_thread.wait()

class ThumbnailLoader(QtCore.QObject):
    loaded = QtCore.pyqtSignal(int, QtGui.QImage)

    @QtCore.pyqtSlot(int, str)
    def load(self, row, path):
        # Image loading and scaling happens safely in the background
        img = QtGui.QImage(path)
        if not img.isNull():
            scaled = img.scaled(QtCore.QSize(250, 250), 
                                QtCore.Qt.AspectRatioMode.KeepAspectRatio, 
                                QtCore.Qt.TransformationMode.SmoothTransformation)
            self.loaded.emit(row, scaled)

A few extra tips:

  • Always use os.path.join instead of concatenating strings with "/" to keep your app compatible with different OS.

  • To fully solve the QThread: Destroyed warning, consider overriding the closeEvent in your main window to explicitly call quit() and wait() on your model's thread.

This should stop the random crashes and make the thumbnail loading smooth.

Q: Retrieving contents on Auto-refresh website A:

You could try the Wayback Machine, paste the URL there and see if the page was archived before the auto-refresh changed the content. If it was never cached or archived anywhere, recovering it is usually not possible.

Q: Workaround for VS Code Flake8 linting failed with KeyError A:

Switching the Flake8 VS Code extension to version 2025.2.0 resolves the error.

Edit: Version 2026.6.0 seems to have resolved the issue.

Q: Is there a way to host a MySQL database and deploy a PHP website using that data for free? A:

Don't do it for free. All free hosting is generally terrible. Pay a little bit for Amazon AWS. It's not that expensive.

Q: How to define reusable styles for content boxes in typst using the cetz package? A:

Use .with() to create a reusable function:

let styled = content.with(frame:"rect",padding:2pt,fill:blue)  

styled((0,0), $x=5$)  
styled((5,0), $z=9$)

https://typst.app/docs/reference/foundations/function/#definitions-with

Or construct an arguments object to reuse:

#let args = arguments(stroke: red, inset: 1em, [Body])
#box(..args)

https://typst.app/docs/reference/foundations/arguments/

Or, the most primitive way I use:

  let wedge = (..args) => edge(
    ..args,
    extrude: (-extrudeRadius,extrudeRadius),
    stroke: (thickness: strokeThickness),
    mark-scale: 180%
  )
  wedge(other args here)
  wedge(other args here)
  wedge(other args here)
